hero.title: Are you really in love?
hero.description: 20 questions to tell love from a crush, and finally know what you feel.

section1.title: Why this question is so hard to settle
section1.p1: If you are looking for an « am I in love » test, something is escaping you. That is entirely normal: nobody teaches us to recognise our own feelings. We know how to describe what we feel for a friend, a brother, a colleague, but as soon as love is involved the vocabulary blurs.
section1.p2: The confusion almost always comes from the same place: intensity. We assume that the stronger it is, the more it must be love. Yet the beginning of a story produces spectacular symptoms, a racing heart, obsessive thoughts, wrecked sleep, which look a lot like love without necessarily being it. Those signals say one thing for certain: this person matters. They do not yet say whether it is a crush or a lasting attachment.
section1.p3: That is exactly what this test tries to separate. It does not measure the intensity of what you feel but its nature: do you love this person, or the picture you have of them? Do you miss their presence, or is it the waiting that thrills you? Twenty questions later you will have a score out of 60 and a clear verdict.

section2.title: The 7 signs that you are in love
section2.intro: No single sign is enough on its own, and the most telling one is not the one you would expect. Here are the ones the test weighs up, from the most obvious to the most decisive.
section2.sign1Text: You think about this person several times a day without deciding to. Their name catches your attention in a conversation. It is the best known sign, but also the least reliable: plain attraction produces exactly the same effect.
section2.sign2Title: They are the first person you want to tell
section2.sign2Text: When something happens to you, good or bad, they are the one you want to tell first. That reaction says far more than butterflies: it means this person has become your reference point.
section2.sign3Text: A week without news does not leave you indifferent. Note the nuance: the missing that belongs to love is calm and steady, whereas anxious missing is something else and points to waiting or insecurity.
section2.sign4Title: You see their flaws and they change nothing
section2.sign4Text: Here is the sign that really separates the two. As long as the person seems perfect to you, you love an image. The day you know their failings, some of them irritate you, and your feelings hold anyway, it is love.
section2.sign5Title: You want their happiness, even without you
section2.sign5Text: The idea of them being happy pleases you, including when that happiness does not run through you. It is the most demanding criterion, the one that separates love from the wish to possess.
section2.sign6Text: You are no longer playing a part or monitoring your image. Paradoxically, that letting go comes later than passion: at the start we try to please, later we dare to be ourselves.
section2.sign7Text: Being able to say nothing together without awkwardness is an excellent marker of real intimacy. As long as a lull makes you uneasy, the stakes still outweigh the bond.

section3.title: How to read your score
section3.intro: Each question is worth 0 to 3 points, for a total out of 60. The most intense answers are not always the ones that score highest: idealising someone or playing a part to please them is worth fewer points than knowing them with their flaws. That is deliberate, and it is what separates love from a crush.
section3.row1Analysis: You like this person, but they do not hold the particular place of someone you are in love with.
section3.row2Analysis: Something is starting. You still love the picture you have of them as much as the real person.
section3.row3Analysis: There is no more room for doubt: you see their flaws and your feelings hold anyway.
section3.row4Analysis: Deep attachment, real knowledge of the other and a wish for their happiness, even without you.

section4.title: Love or plain attraction: telling them apart
section4.intro: The two feel remarkably alike from the inside, especially in the first weeks. Yet five criteria are enough to separate them, and none of them is about intensity.
section4.row2Attraction: Peaks of euphoria and sharp drops.
section4.row3Attraction: It collapses as soon as routine sets in.
section4.row3Love: It handles ordinary days perfectly well.
section4.row4Attraction: You polish your image to please.
section4.row4Love: You dare to be yourself, bad mood included.
section4.row5Attraction: You want it to be with you.
section4.row5Love: You want it, even if it does not run through you.
section4.note: A strong attraction is not a false feeling: it is often the first stage of love. The question is therefore not whether it is « real », but not to make an irreversible decision on the strength of the first three weeks.

section5.title: What is actually happening in your head
section5.p1: The symptoms you feel are not in your imagination: they match phases that are fairly well described, and they do not kick in at the same time or for the same reasons.
section5.p2: Three mechanisms follow and overlap each other.
section5.pillar1Text: At the start the brain runs on anticipation. Every message, every glance triggers a burst of pleasure, and the wait between two contacts amplifies everything. That explains the early euphoria, the missing appetite and the short nights. This phase is powerful, but it is also the least reliable for judging your feelings.
section5.pillar2Text: Attachment, by contrast, is built through repetition and presence. It produces calm rather than excitement, which is precisely why it is less noticeable. Many people believe their feelings are fading when those feelings are simply changing in nature. Our attachment style test shows how this mechanism differs from person to person.
section5.pillar3Text: At the beginning the brain fills in the blanks: whatever we do not know about the other person, we imagine in their favour. That idealisation lasts from a few weeks to a few months, then dissolves. The moment it drops is the real test: either the feelings collapse with it, or they hold, and it was indeed love.

section6.title: The test says you are in love. Now what?
section6.p1: Knowing what you feel settles one question and opens another, often more uncomfortable one: what to do with it, especially when you have no idea whether it is mutual.
section6.p2: A few markers, without the magazine advice.
section6.dont1Text: It never comes. The perfect moment is an elegant way of postponing a frightening conversation indefinitely, and waiting does not make things easier, it only makes them heavier.
section6.dont2Text: Analysing a reply delay or an emoji will teach you nothing reliable. You will always find what you are looking for, one way or the other. Only a real conversation gives a real answer.
section6.do1Text: Spend time together in situations that flatter nobody: a wait, an inconvenience, a day with nothing special in it. Attraction gets bored quickly, love does not. It is the most reliable test there is, and it is free.
section6.do2Text: A solemn declaration intimidates everyone, you first. Saying that this person matters a great deal to you is enough to open the door, without cornering them or exposing yourself more than necessary.
section6.do3Title: Look at what comes back to you
section6.do3Text: The intensity of what you give says nothing about the relationship. Count instead what comes back: the questions you are asked, the effort made to see you, the attention paid to what you say. A living bond shows in that reciprocity.
section6.do4Text: Feelings take time to settle, and that is perfectly fine. If your score sits between two bands, take the test again in a month: the gap between the two results will often tell you more than the score itself.

section7.title: The takeaway
section7.p1: Being in love is not measured by the strength of what you feel, but by what remains once the early excitement subsides. If you know this person's flaws and your feelings hold, the question is settled.
section7.p2: This test is a thinking tool, not a verdict. It gives you a vocabulary and an order of magnitude, nothing more. Nobody, this test included, knows your feelings better than you do: it simply helps put words on what you already half knew.
section7.p3: And if your story is already established, the question becomes a different one: our love or habit test explores what is left of the feelings after several years of living together.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How do I know if I am in love or just attracted?
faq.a1: The most reliable criterion is not intensity but how well you know the other person. As long as they seem perfect to you, what you love is mainly the picture you have of them. When you know their flaws, some of them irritate you and your feelings hold anyway, it is love. A second clue: attraction collapses under routine, love goes through it undamaged.
faq.q2: What is the difference between loving someone and being in love?
faq.a2: Loving someone means caring about them and wanting their good, which also applies to a friend or a family member. Being in love adds desire, exclusivity and the wish for a particular place in their life. That is why you can love a person deeply without being in love with them, and why « I love you but I am not in love with you » is not a contradiction at all.
faq.q3: How long does the early in-love phase last?
faq.a3: The exhilarating phase, the one with obsessive thoughts and idealisation, generally lasts from a few months to around two years. It does not vanish into nothing: it makes way for a calmer, steadier attachment. Many couples read that shift as a loss of feeling when it is really a change of nature.
faq.q4: Can you be in love with someone you barely know?
faq.a4: You can feel a very strong attraction for someone you hardly know, and it is perfectly real. But love in the full sense requires knowing the person, including what makes them imperfect. That is why love at first sight is a possible starting point and never a conclusion.
faq.q5: Is this « am I in love » test reliable?
faq.a5: It is a thinking tool, not a diagnosis. It rests on markers psychologists associate with romantic attachment, but it is only worth what your answers are worth, and your feelings can change from one month to the next. Taking it again a few weeks later is in fact a good way to see which way things are moving.
